name: Host a spawn point
summary: The unit becomes a place where teammates come back into the fight: while it is deployed, switched on or simply alive, teammates who respawn or buy their next unit can choose to appear at it or beside it instead of at base, and in some versions every new unit the team's factory finishes is sent to it. One unit thus carries the team's front line: the host is usually slow, planted or fragile while it hosts, its spawn shows or sounds for the enemy, and killing it cuts off the reinforcements. Versions differ in who may spawn (squad or team), whether the host must deploy, and whether the spawn is the unit itself or a beacon it places. Carrying living teammates is carry-passengers; refilling a squad's lost members is reinforce-squad.
counterplay: Hunt the host: it is usually big, slow or planted while it hosts, and killing it stops the stream of returning enemies at once.
Read the tells: a deployed vehicle on the map, a beacon's beam, dish or beeping, and the flash of each arrival give the spawn away.
Break beacons fast: placed spawn beacons are fragile, any weapon destroys them, and in PlanetSide 2 an EMP grenade clears every beacon around it.
Meet the arrivals: they appear at a known spot, so pre-aimed fire and splash catch the next wave; Call of Duty players camp an enemy's spawn marker for this.
Keep it off the objective: in PlanetSide 2 a host can't deploy inside the no-deploy zones around most objectives, so the ground just outside them is where to look.
Cut a factory relay at either end: when the relaying unit or its factory dies, new units stop reaching the front.

other_examples.note: A flying transport that can switch to a stationary phasing mode; while phased it projects a power field in which units from the player's warp gates warp straight in, and it can power buildings as well. Players bring one along as the reinforcement point of an attack, or set it down at a blind spot to warp in raiders; when the prism dies, the push loses its supply of fresh units.

sources.title: Warp prism, StarCraft Wiki
sources.note: The phasing-mode description sits in the ability box the page includes (Template:SC2WarpPrism, read the same day).

shooter_analogues.unit: Sunderer and the Advanced Mobile Station
shooter_analogues.note: The big ground transport (and, with modules, the Galaxy, the Colossus and the ANT) deploys on a key into a mobile spawn station: while deployed it can't move, any allied soldier may spawn at it, and it offers equipment terminals. It can't deploy inside the no-deploy zones placed around most objectives, nor close to another deployed station. Separately, squad logistics lets the squadmates of anyone aboard spawn into one of its seats at any time.

Any member of a squad can plant the squad's one beacon, which needs open sky above it and sends a coloured laser upward; squadmates who choose it come down by pod from high above. Planting a new one removes the old one, and the same player must wait a long time to plant again. It breaks under most damage, an EMP grenade destroys every beacon near it, and squad leaders can stop the rest of the squad, or chosen fireteams, from carrying and placing beacons.

shooter_analogues.unit: Radio Beacon (Battlefield 3 and 4) and Squad Leader Spawn Beacon (Battlefield 2142)
shooter_analogues.note: A recon gadget that gives the recon's squad an extra spawn wherever it is planted; outdoors on maps with aircraft, squadmates who pick it arrive by parachute from high up. Its dish and beeping make it hard to hide, any weapon destroys it, it vanishes once its owner respawns, and the owner earns a bonus each time a squadmate uses it. The earlier Battlefield 2142 beacon belonged to the squad leader, dropped squadmates in pods, needed open sky and stopped working once the team held no control points.

sources.title: Radio Beacon, Battlefield Wiki
sources.note: Quotes the Battlelog descriptions of the Battlefield 3 and Battlefield 4 gadgets.

sources.title: Squad Leader Spawn Beacon, Battlefield Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: An engineer builds a rally point the whole team can spawn at; it breaks easily and makes a beeping sound that only enemies hear. APC squads serve as mobile rally points instead: small arms can't destroy them, but they make a big target and need longer between spawns.

The marine commander's respawn building: while powered, each portal brings one dead marine back at a time after a short materialisation, so more portals mean faster waves, and a commander adds portals before a big push. Aliens rush them, above all early in a round.

sources.title: Infantry Portal (Natural Selection 2), Natural Selection Wiki

shooter_analogues.note: Any living squadmate can call dead teammates back into the mission; the squad shares a pool of uses that grows with the number of players, enemy jammers block the call, and the returning player lands in a pod that can hit enemies near the landing.

Equipment that sets the player's own next spawn where it is placed: a flare or small beacon shown green to friends and red to enemies, who can destroy it by shooting it or using it. Spawning on a known marker invites spawn-camping, so Black Ops let players cancel the insertion between lives.

sources.title: Tactical Insertion, Call of Duty Wiki

player_translation.summary: Deploy with Q and you become the team's forward spawn: teammates on the respawn screen see you on the map and can choose to appear beside you instead of at base. While you host you are planted and marked for the enemy, so you pick a hidden spot near the fight, and the enemy hunts you to cut the stream.
as_user: Your job is placement: find a spot close to the fight but out of its sight lines, deploy, and watch teammates pour out beside you.
While hosting you can't move (or move only slowly, in moving variants), and each arrival flashes, so packing up and moving before the enemy finds you is half the skill.
You earn points for every teammate who spawns on you, so hosting pays without kills.
Beacon variant: you plant a small beacon instead of hosting yourself and stay free to fight, but the beacon is fragile and gives itself away.
Factory-relay variant: every unit your team buys appears beside you, so you lead the push and the reinforcements come to you.
as_target: A deployed host is the most valuable target on the map: one flank or one strike on it stops a whole wave of returning enemies.
Arrivals get a moment of protection, so firing at the spawn ring wastes ammo; kill the host, or catch them as they step out.
Beacons have a beam and a sound; follow them and break the beacon with any weapon or an EMP.
If you can't reach the host, hold the ground near objectives where hosts aren't allowed to deploy.
teammates: Teammates pick the host on the respawn screen, so a well-placed host decides where the whole team fights.
Escorts guard it: planted and slow, the host lives only as long as someone watches its flanks.
Scouts warn the host when enemies approach so it can pack up and move.
On the other side, flankers and scouts hunt hosts and beacons, and a joint strike on the host breaks the push it feeds.
controls: Q (deploy): plant and start hosting; Q again packs up, with a short delay each way.
Respawning teammates: hosts appear as icons on the respawn map with their health and a 'contested' tag; clicking one spawns there after the usual wait.
Beacon variant: Q plants the beacon at your feet (open sky needed for pod or parachute arrivals); only one beacon per player, with a long wait to replace it.
Factory-relay variant: R toggles whether teammates' new units come to you or to base.
feedback: A tall team-coloured beam or ring over a deployed host or a planted beacon, readable from above by both teams nearby.
A flash and sound at each arrival, which nearby enemies hear.
Host HUD: a counter of teammates who spawned on you, a warning when enemies come close, and a 'can't deploy here' notice inside no-deploy zones.
Respawn screen: each host's icon with its health and whether enemies are near it.
changes_from_rts: RTS units don't respawn, so the Vimana's Gate Link moves fresh production to the unit; in a buy-and-become shooter the same idea becomes teammates choosing to respawn, or to buy their next unit, at the host.
Gate Link works while the Vimana flies anywhere; a host that spawns teammates on the move is too strong for the base version, which must deploy, as PlanetSide 2's stations do.
No-deploy zones around objectives, a minimum distance between hosts and a wait between spawns keep hosts from turning objectives into spawn camps.
Arrivals get brief protection and a spread of spawn spots, so a known spawn can't simply be farmed.
The Vimana dies with its home Gate; the player version keeps the host's own life as the only link that matters, so the counterplay stays on the field.

team_play.notes: All of its value is for teammates: the host decides where the team re-enters the fight, teammates guard it because it is planted and fragile while hosting, and the enemy team must find and kill it together to stop the waves it feeds.

notes: Ties into the respawn screen: hosts listed on the map, their state (health, contested, blocked) and a choice that respects respawn timers.
Safe spawn spots around the host for several players at once, with no clipping into walls, vehicles or each other, and brief spawn protection.
Deploy rules: no-deploy zones, a minimum spacing between hosts, and packing up under fire.
Beacon variants need a fragile placeable with its own health, a one-per-player limit and pod or parachute arrivals.
The factory-relay variant reroutes teammates' purchases to a moving unit and must handle the host dying mid-delivery.
A forward spawn close to an objective can decide a match on its own; no-deploy zones and spacing are the main levers.
Spawn-camping cuts both ways: hosts can drown a defence in arrivals, and campers can farm a known spawn.
A host that spawns teammates while moving (the Vimana's version) makes the whole team as mobile as one unit; keep it to high-spice variants.
Rewards per spawn can tempt players to host instead of fighting; that is fine as a role, but caps keep it honest.
Enemies must see where the reinforcements come from: hosts and beacons need clear beams and arrival flashes.
Several hosts and beacons on one screen confuse; team colours and a cap per team keep them apart.
Players need to tell a host from an ordinary transport at a glance, since one carries living teammates and the other brings back the dead.

variants.name: Deployed station
variants.summary: Stop and deploy to become a spawn point for the whole team, often with a resupply terminal; while deployed you can't move, and packing up takes a moment.
variants.seen_in: PlanetSide 2 Sunderer (Advanced Mobile Station); StarCraft II Warp Prism (Phasing Mode)

variants.name: Squad spawns aboard
variants.summary: Squadmates of anyone aboard can spawn straight into a free seat while you drive, with no deploying; the vehicle is a moving squad spawn but holds only as many as it has seats.
variants.seen_in: PlanetSide 2 squad logistics on the Sunderer and other vehicles

variants.name: Placed beacon
variants.summary: Plant a small beacon, one at a time with a long wait to replace it, that your squad or team can spawn at; it gives itself away with a beam or beeping and breaks under any fire.
variants.seen_in: Battlefield 3 and 4 Radio Beacon; Battlefield 2142 Squad Leader Spawn Beacon; PlanetSide 2 Spawn Beacon; Enlisted rally points

countered_by.why: An EMP blast destroys every spawn beacon around it at once (PlanetSide 2).
Scouts find beacons by their beam and beeping and break them before the squad can use them (reasoned from the tells the beacon pages describe).

variants.name: Arrive by pod or parachute
variants.summary: Teammates who spawn on you or your beacon come down from high above by pod or parachute, steering a little toward it; they can be shot on the way down, and the spot needs open sky.
variants.seen_in: PlanetSide 2 Spawn Beacon; Battlefield 2142 squad beacon; Battlefield 3 and 4 Radio Beacon outdoors; Helldivers 2 Reinforce

variants.name: Factory relay
variants.summary: A toggle: while it is on, every unit your team buys (or every unit of one kind, such as aircraft) appears beside you, even while you move, instead of at base.
variants.seen_in: Tempest Rising Vimana (Gate Link); StarCraft II Warp Prism warp-ins

variants.name: Call in the fallen
variants.summary: No standing spawn: on a key you call dead teammates back down beside you, spending one use from a pool the whole team shares; enemy jammers block the call.

variants.name: Personal spawn marker
variants.summary: Place a marker where only you will respawn next time; enemies see it glowing and can break it or wait beside it, so you may cancel it from the respawn screen.

adds_strengths.why: Comes back next to the objective it was fighting for instead of at base.
Teammates who respawn can appear at it, so the team re-enters the fight at the front instead of walking from base.

adds_weaknesses.why: While it hosts it is planted or slowed and its spawns give it away, so it becomes the enemy team's first target.

countered_by.why: Fast flankers reach a planted host behind the lines and kill it before it can pack up (reasoned: hosts can't move while they host).
Long-range fire and bombardment hit a host that can't dodge while it hosts (reasoned from the deployed state).

open_questions: May a host take spawns while it moves, as Gate Link does, or only while deployed? (Recommended: deployed in the base version; moving hosts only in the factory-relay variant.)
Who may spawn on a host: its squad, or the whole team?
Should spawning on a host be blocked while enemies stand close to it, or should arrivals get a short spawn protection instead?
Should hosts earn points per teammate who spawns on them, as Battlefield's beacons pay their owners, and does that need a cap?
In a buy-and-become game, may teammates buy a different unit at the host, or only come back as the unit they had?

shooter_fit.reason: Forward spawns are a staple of team shooters (PlanetSide 2's stations, Battlefield's beacons, Enlisted's rally points) and give a whole team a reason to guard one unit; from above a planted host and its arrival flashes read clearly. It needs no-deploy zones and spawn protection.
